name: Ivan Walsh

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the independent Work Futures Panel, and your answers are confidential. What does an ordinary day at the accounting firm involve?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 58 and an experienced accountant with a bachelor’s degree and professional accountancy qualification, preparing accounts and returns for produce wholesalers. I like tracing a short delivery back to its signed slip; I dislike finding that a rushed invoice copied the wrong weight all the way into a return. Beth and I have grown children and barely three weeks of costs saved, so I am thinking about retirement without pretending it can pay this month’s rent.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A small AI saving feels like the invoice sorting I already do for produce wholesalers. I use AI each day to group delivery questions, then check the weighbridge slip against the buyer’s account.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell clients the delivered weight still has to match a signed slip. A fast draft that charges for missing crates is a poor service.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My accountant pay is below the usual rate, and my partner Beth and I have about three weeks of costs saved. I am experienced at this desk, but there are few similar firms nearby and rent is due whether software helps or not.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep preparing assigned accounts and tax returns, marking each AI mismatch in my delivery notebook. If groceries leave room after payday, I would transfer eight from my wage into an emergency envelope rather than count the existing savings twice.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the little margin we already have. A quiet week at the wholesalers can leave my own paid hours light even without major AI change.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What did the sorter miss yesterday?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The AI sorter accepted twelve crates even though the signed delivery slip said ten. I called the buyer and corrected the invoice before the tax return went out.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Where would the eight come from?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Beth works morning shifts at the school kitchen, and her pay helps with rent but cannot carry both of us. The eight is a new transfer only when groceries are paid.

say: I would require **signed delivery slips** for charged crates.
I would keep a **mismatch notebook** beside AI sorted invoices.
think: Lower pay and **three weeks saved** make rent a present pressure.
Few nearby firms leave little room for a **lost shift**.
do: Keep preparing **assigned produce accounts** and checking daily AI groups against signed slips.
Transfer **eight from wages** after payday only if groceries allow.
feel: **Anxious** about rent and current variable paid hours.
S0.quote: The AI sorter accepted twelve crates even though the signed delivery slip said ten.
fieldNote: The **twelve-crate error** gives his daily AI habit a concrete safeguard: a signed weighbridge and delivery record.
Lower pay, **three weeks saved** and few nearby employers make him anxious before any large technological shock.

steps.text: Keep assigned produce returns and check daily AI groups against signed slips
Transfer eight from wages after payday only if groceries allow

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If software writes and checks most tax returns, my years with produce invoices will not keep every paid hour. The later robots may change the warehouse, but our accounts desk changes sooner.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the firm to show the error count before raising targets. I would also ask our trade association for a clear name on every automated return.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my own paid week could shrink and the three-week envelope would go fast. Beth’s school-kitchen wage covers a piece of rent, not the whole household.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask my supervisor Rina for two paid supervised sessions learning the new delivery-reconciliation screen on closed accounts, and complete them if approved. If refused, I will keep current paid invoices only while offered and practise on free sample slips.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about possibly losing wage hours I cannot replace nearby. I am quick with tools, but a tool has to earn its place on a live client account.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: When would the new screen be ready for live files?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would use the new screen on live accounts only after Rina signs a report that all planted wrong weights were found and client data stayed private. I would take the count to the trade association meeting.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Where would you look after a cut?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If my paid hours actually fall, I will apply for posted accounts work at the produce depot only with written pay covering rent and food, confirmed start and hours that fit Beth’s morning shifts. A family contact at the produce depot cannot promise me a wage.

say: I would ask for **error counts** before targets rise.
I would demand a **named signer** for automated returns through the trade association.
think: My own **paid week** may shrink despite years of experience with produce accounts.
Beth’s kitchen wage and **three weeks saved** cannot replace my income or cover rent for long.
do: Learn **screen** in two Rina-approved paid supervised sessions; use live only after all planted wrong weights found and client privacy cleared.
If hours fall, seek **posted depot-accounts** with written pay covering rent and food, confirmed start and Beth-compatible hours; keep invoices while paid.
Bring the **error count** to the trade association and ask for named signers.
feel: **Anxious** about a possible cut to my paid week.
S1.quote: A family contact at the produce depot cannot promise me a wage.
fieldNote: The **new screen** needs paid supervised closed-file practice and a signed error and privacy gate before live use.
He will use **association accountability** and seek a posted depot opening only after actual lost hours with written household fitting terms.

steps.text: Learn screen in two supervised paid sessions; use live after Rina signs all-error/privacy pass
If refused, practise free slips while assigned paid invoices remain
If hours fall, seek posted depot-accounts: written pay covering rent and food, confirmed start, Beth-compatible hours
Bring error count to trade association and demand named signers

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Full AGI in 2028 would do the thinking in our accounts before 2031 robots changed loading work. Even a produce counter uses ordering and invoices that AGI could handle in 2028.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the firm for written last-pay dates and tell growers to keep signed delivery records. I would not claim a counter job is safe simply because people still lift crates.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my paid accounts work to end in the first year after AGI. Three weeks saved and Beth’s kitchen wage cannot keep rent and food covered for long.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would cancel our paid film package at renewal and send its released monthly fee into emergency cash. After 2028 job loss, I will apply for posted depot receiving shifts only with written pay covering rent and food, confirmed hours and a start date; I will take paid firm closeout files only while offered.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed because I expect my own wage to stop. I can carry crates, but I cannot count on a vacancy before the robots arrive.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which bill would you actually stop?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our paid film package renews in January and costs less than the rent, but it is one bill we can actually stop. I would tell Beth before cancelling because we watch together after her shift.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would receiving last longer than accounts?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Weighing and moving crates are hands-on for now, while the depot ordering screen faces AGI immediately. I would treat receiving as a posted paid bridge, not a permanent escape.

say: I would seek **written last-pay dates** for the tax desk.
I would tell growers **depot ordering** faces AGI before robots.
think: I expect my **accounts wage** to stop after 2028.
Three weeks saved and Beth’s wage cannot carry **rent and food**.
do: Cancel the **film package** at January renewal and save only its released monthly fee.
After job loss, seek **posted receiving** with written pay covering rent and food, confirmed hours and start; take closeout only while paid.
Ask the **firm** for written last-pay dates as the accounts work ends.
feel: **Alarmed** about expected wage loss and a thin reserve.
S2.quote: Our paid film package renews in January and costs less than the rent, but it is one bill we can actually stop.
fieldNote: The **film package** yields new monthly cash only after cancellation, with no claim that existing savings grew.
Depot **ordering and invoices** face 2028 AGI; physical crate work may last until robots arrive around 2031.

steps.text: Cancel film package in January and save released monthly fee
Take paid firm closeout files only while offered
After 2028 loss, seek posted receiving: written pay covering rent and food, confirmed hours and start
Ask firm for written last-pay dates on accounts work

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years to 2031 gives me time to try a paid physical part of the produce chain, although the ordering desk still faces AGI in 2031. Robots around 2034 could then take more loading work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the depot to advertise paid trainee places with real supervisors. I would not sell my family a vague apprenticeship as an income plan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I might still need to work well past 63, since we have no confirmed retirement figure to cover rent. The three-week reserve will not fund an unpaid change of trade.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would check posted depot goods-receiving trainee places each month and take a supervised loading-and-inventory cycle only if the employer funds fees, pays training hours and provides written rent-covering wages, start and shifts. If no suitable place opens, I will study free stock ledgers while keeping assigned paid returns only while the firm offers them, including after 2031.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious because five years gives me time to try, but I cannot carry the household through an unpaid course. I know robots may shorten this route later.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would a goods-receiving cycle teach?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: One cycle would mean counting a delivered pallet and matching it to the buyer’s order with a supervisor. I would need hands-on practice, not just a video about warehouse safety.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the trainee terms do not fit?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If the posted trainee wage is too low or its shift clashes with Beth’s mornings, I would stay with paid accounts while offered and keep checking notices. A later robot date does not make the depot paperwork safe until then.

say: I would ask for **posted paid trainee places** with supervisors.
I would separate **2031 ordering risk** from 2034 loading robots.
think: I cannot assume **retirement money** pays rent at 63.
Three weeks saved cannot fund an **unpaid trade change**.
do: Complete a **supervised depot cycle** only in a posted paid place with funded fees, paid time and written rent-covering terms.
If no suitable place opens, study **free stock ledgers** while paid tax work remains assigned.
feel: **Anxious** about an unpaid gap, with time to seek real practice.
S3.quote: One cycle would mean counting a delivered pallet and matching it to the buyer’s order with a supervisor.
fieldNote: The **depot trainee route** is actual hands-on practice, contingent on posted work, funded fees, paid supervision and adequate written terms.
He recognises **2031 desk ordering** and 2034 physical automation separately; free ledgers and offered paid returns are the fallback.

steps.text: Complete posted depot cycle with funded fees, paid training, supervision and written rent-covering wage/start/shifts
Study free stock ledgers while assigned paid returns remain after 2031
Check posted depot trainee roles monthly; accept only written rent-covering pay, start and Beth-compatible shifts

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans."

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten years to 2036 makes me 68, and I hope Beth and I can slow down then. Our accounts desk still meets AGI in 2036; hands-on depot robots would follow around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell younger staff to learn how the actual goods arrive, not only how software names them. I would ask our firm for yearly paid-hour plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I cannot promise we will have enough confirmed income to stop working in 2036. The three weeks saved now and Beth’s school wage are not a retirement calculation.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep assigned paid returns while they last and put ten from each monthly wage toward our small kitchen repair debt if rent and food allow. After 2036, only if verified income still leaves a gap and the firm cuts my paid files, I would seek posted depot receiving with written pay covering that gap, start and workable shifts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious now because ten years does not improve this month’s rent by itself. I would be alarmed if paid accounts ended while the gap remained.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What makes the extra payment possible?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten is new cash from this month’s wage, not the little reserve we have. I would stop the extra debt payment if Beth lost kitchen hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you ask your daughter to help?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our grown daughter can visit us for supper, but I would not build our later budget around her wage. I want a real written offer if I still need paid work.

say: I would ask for **yearly paid-hour plans** at the firm.
I would tell juniors to understand **physical deliveries** as well as software.
think: I cannot count **unconfirmed later income** as money available for rent in 2036.
Three weeks saved leave our **present household margin** narrow even before AGI arrives.
do: Keep **assigned paid returns** while offered and pay ten extra monthly on kitchen debt only if rent and food allow.
After 2036 cuts, seek **posted depot receiving** only if income gap remains, with written gap-covering pay, start and shifts.
Ask the **firm yearly** for its paid-hour plan before deciding how long to work.
feel: **Anxious** now from thin cash; alarmed if paid files end.
S4.quote: Our grown daughter can visit us for supper, but I would not build our later budget around her wage.
fieldNote: The **extra debt payment** comes from wages and stops if Beth’s paid hours or essential bills change.
The **post-2036 search** requires verified wage need, real paid-file loss and a posted offer; no pension is assumed.

steps.text: Keep assigned paid returns only while firm offers them
Pay extra ten monthly on kitchen debt if bills allow; stop if Beth loses hours
After 2036 cuts, seek posted receiving only if gap; require written gap-covering pay/start/shifts
Ask firm yearly for paid-hour plans on produce accounts

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because my paid accounts could end before a depot wage begins. Written last-pay dates and a real posted receiving place with enough pay would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask why I keep the signed weighbridge slips. A buyer should not pay tax on two crates that never crossed the gate.

headlineQuote: A buyer should not pay tax on two crates that never crossed the gate.
portrait: Ivan is a **58 year old experienced** accountant with a bachelor’s degree and professional qualification who handles produce accounts and returns.
He uses **AI daily** for invoice groups but checks signed delivery weights and knows the sorter can repeat a wrong count.
Lower pay, Beth’s kitchen wage, grown children, **three weeks saved** and few local firms make his baseline anxious.
He explores **paid depot receiving** as a bridge while recognising AGI reaches ordering first and robots follow later.
biggestWorry: The **2028 AGI** picture could end his paid produce accounts before another wage begins.
whatWouldHelp: **Written last-pay dates** and a posted receiving place with adequate written wages would help.
